newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish PM Lipponen calls February confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Finnish PM Lipponen calls February confidence vote.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said late on Thursday that a parliamentary vote in February on a bill to liberalise retail store opening hours will also be a confidence vote in his government.
Lipponen called the confidence vote after parliament earlier on Thursday had rejected the opening hours bill, handing the left-right-green government an unexpected defeat.
Lipponen said the government would introduce the rejected bill again and parliament will deal with it in February when it reconvenes after the Christmas recess.
"The slate will be wiped clean in February when MPs of the government parties will have to make up their minds on the basis that this will be a vote of confidence," Lipponen told Finnish media.
The bill was narrowly rejected, by 84 votes to 82. Of the five government parties' 142 MPs, 36 voted against the proposal. Of those, 20 were from Lipponen's own Social Democratic Party.

Some commentators said the defeat -- Lipponen cabinet's first significant setback in parliament -- was an indication of growing criticism among left-wing MPs of right-leaning fiscal austerity policies.

The outcome also highlighted the influence in the SDP camp of MPs with strong trade union ties. Many unions quietly support the shop workers' union, which is fiercely opposed to liberalised retail store opening hours.

Analysts say union support for the government's outspoken goal to see Finland among the first to enter the third stage of Economic and Monetary Union in 1999 will be crucial to ensure that the SDP parliamentary group will back the project.
The Finnish parliament is scheduled to vote late in 1997 or early in 1998 on whether Finland should take part in EMU.
